newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wants 35 BAe Hawks - source.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wants 35 BAe Hawks - source.

text.p: The Australian government is negotiating for 35 British Aerospace Plc Hawk attack-trainer aircraft, a source close to the talks told Reuters on Wednesday.

Since choosing British Aerospace as preferred contractor to fill the trainer requirement, Canberra has refused to say exactly how many aircraft it would buy, defining the requirement only as "up to 40".
But the source said negotiations had settled on 35 aircraft.
British Aerospace has said it would deliver only the first 12 aircraft complete.
The remainder would be assembled in Australia.
Earlier on Wednesday Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said Australia had chosen the Rolls-Royce Plc Adour, the standard Hawk engine, to power its aircraft.
The Defence Department rejected a rival bid from AlliedSignal Inc, which had hoped that Australia would launch its F124 engine on the Hawk, a top-selling aircraft.
The department selected British Aerospace as preferred contractor in November.
The final contract is expected to be signed this year.
